Full implementation in reference file.\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Dev mode requires &#96;'unsafe-eval'&#96;** for React error stack traces and &#96;'unsafe-inline'&#96; for Tailwind HMR — NOT in production\\\\\\\\n- **CSP makes pages dynamically rendered** — nonces change per request, so CSP pages cannot be statically generated\\\\\\\\n- **If adding third-party scripts**, add their domains to &#96;script-src&#96; and &#96;connect-src&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Read the nonce** in Server Components via &#96;(await headers()).get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"x-nonce\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\")&#96; for &#96;\u003cScript\u003e&#96; tags\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003e Full &#96;proxy.ts&#96; CSP implementation and CSP directives reference: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#csp-full-implementation)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Security Headers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSix headers configured in &#96;next.config.ts&#96; via the &#96;headers()&#96; function:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Header | Purpose |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: on&#96; | DNS prefetching for external links |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;Strict-Transport-Security&#96; | Forces HTTPS for 2 years, all subdomains, preload-eligible |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN&#96; | Prevents iframe embedding (clickjacking) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff&#96; | Prevents MIME-type sniffing |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin&#96; | Limits referrer info on cross-origin |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;Permissions-Policy&#96; | Disables camera, microphone, geolocation, browsing-topics |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Do NOT add &#96;X-XSS-Protection&#96;** — deprecated, can introduce vulnerabilities. CSP replaces it\\\\\\\\n- **Do NOT set &#96;Cache-Control&#96; for &#96;_next/static&#96;** — Next.js handles immutable caching automatically\\\\\\\\n- **HSTS preload** — only submit to preload list after confirming HTTPS on all subdomains (irreversible)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003e Full &#96;next.config.ts&#96; headers implementation: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#security-headers-implementation)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Auth Protection Pattern\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTwo-layer approach as recommended by [better-auth Next.js docs](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next#auth-protection):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Layer 1 — Optimistic redirects via &#96;proxy.ts&#96;** (UX only, NOT secure):\\\\\\\\n- Checks cookie existence only — no DB call, no session validation\\\\\\\\n- Logged-in users on &#96;/login&#96; → redirect to &#96;/dashboard&#96;\\\\\\\\n- Logged-out users on &#96;/dashboard&#96; → redirect to &#96;/login&#96;\\\\\\\\n- Anyone can forge a cookie — this layer is purely for avoiding page flash\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Layer 2 — Real auth in every page/action** (the actual security):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n// Every protected page and Server Action must do this:\\\\\\\\nconst session = await getServerSession();\\\\\\\\nif (!session) redirect(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"/login\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\");\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;getServerSession()&#96; in &#96;lib/server-session.ts&#96; validates the session against the database, wrapped in &#96;cache()&#96; to deduplicate within a request.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"const cspHeader = &#96;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":34},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  default-src 'self';\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":35},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${isDev ? — see [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Zod Schemas](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#2-server-action-hardening-strategy-like).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Validate on the server** — client-side validation is UX only; the Server Action is the security boundary\\\\\\\\n- **Use &#96;.safeParse()&#96;** — graceful error handling without try-catch\\\\\\\\n- **Set max lengths** — prevent DoS via long inputs; match DB column constraints\\\\\\\\n- **Use &#96;.or(z.literal(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"))&#96; for optional URL fields** — empty form strings aren't valid URLs\\\\\\\\n- **Transform empty strings to &#96;undefined&#96;** via &#96;.transform()&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## SQL Injection Prevention\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDrizzle ORM produces parameterized queries by default. Safe patterns:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\ndb.select().from(projects).where(eq(projects.id, id));       // Query builder — safe\\\\\\\\ndb.insert(projects).values({ title, description });           // Insert — safe\\\\\\\\nsql\u003cnumber\u003e&#96;COALESCE(MAX(${projects.order}), 0)&#96;              // sql template — safe (parameterized)\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Never do**:\\\\\\\\n- &#96;db.execute(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\&#96;SELECT * FROM projects WHERE id = ${id}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\&#96;)&#96; — SQL injection\\\\\\\\n- &#96;sql.raw(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\&#96;... WHERE title = '${title}'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\&#96;)&#96; — SQL injection\\\\\\\\n- Dynamic table/column names from user input\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Always use the Drizzle query builder** or &#96;sql&#96; template literal\\\\\\\\n- **Never use &#96;sql.raw()&#96; with user input**\\\\\\\\n- **Validate IDs as numbers before queries** — even though Drizzle parameterizes\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Secure Environment Variables\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Pattern | Exposure | Examples |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_*&#96; | Bundled in client JS (visible to everyone) | &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL&#96; |\\\\\\\\n| No prefix | Server-only (never sent to browser) | &#96;TURSO_DATABASE_URL&#96;, &#96;TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN&#96;, &#96;BETTER_AUTH_SECRET&#96; |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **NEVER prefix secrets with &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_&#96;**\\\\\\\\n- **NEVER commit &#96;.env.local&#96; to git** — verify &#96;.gitignore&#96; includes it\\\\\\\\n- **Generate &#96;BETTER_AUTH_SECRET&#96;** with &#96;openssl rand -base64 32&#96; (at least 32 chars)\\\\\\\\n- **On Vercel, use Sensitive Environment Variables** — encrypted, non-readable after creation\\\\\\\\n- **Use different values per environment** (Production, Preview, Development)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## CSRF Protection\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **better-auth verifies &#96;Origin&#96; header** on all mutation requests — rejects if origin doesn't match &#96;trustedOrigins&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Next.js Server Actions are protected by default** — framework validates &#96;Origin&#96; header; no additional CSRF tokens needed\\\\\\\\n- **Do NOT set &#96;disableCSRFCheck: true&#96;** or &#96;disableOriginCheck: true&#96; in better-auth\\\\\\\\n- **Session cookies use &#96;SameSite: 'lax'&#96;** by default — allows top-level navigations, blocks cross-site form submissions\\\\\\\\n- **Custom API routes** (beyond &#96;/api/auth/*&#96;) need manual CSRF token verification\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Secure Cookies \u0026 Sessions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nbetter-auth manages session cookies with flags: &#96;httpOnly: true&#96;, &#96;secure: true&#96; (production), &#96;sameSite: 'lax'&#96;, &#96;path: '/'&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Never access session cookies in client JavaScript** — &#96;httpOnly&#96; by design\\\\\\\\n- **Cookie cache (5 min)** — revoked session valid up to 5 minutes; acceptable for single-admin dashboard\\\\\\\\n- **Don't implement custom session timeout** — better-auth handles expiration/renewal\\\\\\\\n- **Custom cookies** must always set: &#96;httpOnly&#96;, &#96;secure&#96;, &#96;sameSite&#96;, reasonable &#96;maxAge&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Rate Limiting\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Use Vercel WAF as the primary rate limiting layer** — operates at the edge with global state, before your code runs. In-memory counters (LRU, Map, better-auth &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"memory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; storage) are unreliable on serverless — instances don't share memory, cold starts reset counters.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Recommended WAF Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rule | Path | Limit | Window | Action |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Auth protection | &#96;/api/auth/*&#96; | 20 req | 60s | Deny (429) |\\\\\\\\n| General API | &#96;/api/*&#96; | 100 req | 60s | Deny (429) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Enable better-auth rate limiting** as defense in depth — use &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; storage for production, &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"memory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; acceptable as basic deterrent for low-traffic single-admin\\\\\\\\n- **Stricter limits on auth endpoints** (10-20 req/min) — most targeted\\\\\\\\n- **Return &#96;429 Too Many Requests&#96;** with &#96;Retry-After&#96; header when possible\\\\\\\\n- **Use &#96;@vercel/firewall&#96; SDK** for application-level context (user ID, etc.) — requires matching dashboard rule\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003e Full &#96;@vercel/firewall&#96; before every deployment** — no high/critical vulnerabilities\\\\\\\\n- **&#96;pnpm up&#96; weekly** (within semver ranges), &#96;pnpm dlx npm-check-updates&#96; monthly (check majors)\\\\\\\\n- **Lock file is your friend** — always commit &#96;pnpm-lock.yaml&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Ignore unfixable CVEs explicitly** in &#96;auditConfig.ignoreCves&#96; to find oversized dependencies\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Server vs Client Decision Tree\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\nIs the component interactive (onClick, onChange, state, effects)?\\\\\\\\n├── NO → Server Component (default, no directive)\\\\\\\\n│   - Zero client JS, direct DB access, secrets stay on server\\\\\\\\n│\\\\\\\\n└── YES → Does the ENTIRE component need interactivity?\\\\\\\\n    ├── NO → Split: data fetching in Server Component, pass props to Client\\\\\\\\n    └── YES → Client Component (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use client\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\")\\\\\\\\n        - Keep small, import into Server parent, never fetch data inside\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Project-Specific Boundaries\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Component | Type | Reason |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Dashboard layout | Server | Static structure |\\\\\\\\n| Sidebar navigation | Client | Active state, mobile toggle |\\\\\\\\n| Projects list page | Server | Data fetching, table rendering |\\\\\\\\n| Delete confirmation dialog | Client | Modal state, click handlers |\\\\\\\\n| Login form | Client | Form state, submission |\\\\\\\\n| Public portfolio page | Server | Static rendering, SEO |\\\\\\\\n| Skills multi-select | Client | Combobox interactivity (cmdk) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Core Web Vitals\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — Loading\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rating | Threshold |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Good | \u003c= 2.5s |\\\\\\\\n| Needs Improvement | 2.5s–4.0s |\\\\\\\\n| Poor | \u003e 4.0s |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Optimizations in this project**: &#96;priority&#96; on above-fold images, &#96;next/font&#96; for fonts, &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; + &#96;cacheLife&#96; for data, Server Components on public page, &#96;loading.tsx&#96; for instant shell.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — Interactivity\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rating | Threshold |\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"## Bundle Optimization\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":130},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":131},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"### &#96;optimizePackageImports&#96;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":132},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":133},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Already configured in &#96;next.config.ts&#96; Perfect for dynamic lists and grids.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8029},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Layout Animation Example:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8030},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8031},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8032},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"function LayoutAnimation() {\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8033},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  const [items, setItems] = useState([1, 2, 3]);\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8034}]},\\\\\\\"score\\\\\\\":0.20882189273834229},{\\\\\\\"codeBlock\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"relativeWorkspacePath\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-12-01_10-48Z-static-portfolio-website-design-specifications.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"range\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"startPosition\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"endPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":18}},\\\\\\\"contents\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --\u003e\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003c!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --\u003e\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nInterprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCreate a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system \u0026 visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing \u0026 grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance \u0026 best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Import Tailwind in your CSS with &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;, not &#96;@tailwind&#96; directives.- Define design tokens, custom utilities, and settings in CSS using the new &#96;@theme&#96; at-rule and related directives (so there is no default &#96;tailwind.config.ts&#96;). If you intentionally want to keep a legacy JS/TS configuration, load it explicitly from CSS using &#96;@config \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"./tailwind.config.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (this is allowed for backward compatibility), but prefer CSS-first. - Use &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; for PostCSS setups or &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; when using Vite/Next dev tooling. Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system \u0026 visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing \u0026 grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance \u0026 best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). shadcn.io Component Library\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nshadcn.io is a comprehensive React UI component library built on shadcn/ui principles, providing developers with production-ready, composable components for modern web applications. The library serves as a centralized resource for React developers who need high-quality UI components with TypeScript support, ranging from basic interactive elements to advanced AI-powered integrations. Unlike traditional component libraries that require package installations, shadcn.io components are designed to be copied directly into your project, giving you full control and customization capabilities.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe library encompasses four major categories: composable UI components (terminal, dock, credit cards, QR codes, color pickers), chart components built with Recharts, animation components with Tailwind CSS integration, and custom React hooks for state management and lifecycle operations. Each component follows best practices for accessibility, performance, and developer experience, with comprehensive TypeScript definitions and Next.js compatibility. The platform emphasizes flexibility and customization, allowing developers to modify components at the source level rather than being constrained by package APIs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Core Components\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Terminal Component\\\\\\\\nInteractive terminal emulator with typing animations and command execution simulation for developer-focused interfaces.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { Terminal } from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/ui/terminal\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default function DemoTerminal() {\\\\\\\\n return (\\\\\\\\n npm install @repo/terminalInstalling dependencies...npm start\\\\\\\\n )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Dock Component\\\\\\\\nmacOS-style application dock with smooth magnification effects on hover, perfect for navigation menus.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { Dock, DockIcon } from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/ui/dock\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nimport { Home, Settings, User, Mail } from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"lucide-react\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default function AppDock() {\\\\\\\\n return (\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Credit Card Component\\\\\\\\nInteractive 3D credit card component with flip animations for payment forms and card displays.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { CreditCard } from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"@/components/ui/credit-card\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# shadcn.io Component Library\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"shadcn.io is a comprehensive React UI component library built on shadcn/ui principles, providing developers with production-ready, composable components for modern web applications. The library serves as a centralized resource for React developers who need high-quality UI components with TypeScript support, ranging from basic interactive elements to advanced AI-powered integrations. Unlike traditional component libraries that require package installations, shadcn.io components are designed to be copied directly into your project, giving you full control and customization capabilities.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"The library encompasses four major categories: composable UI components (terminal, dock, credit cards, QR codes, color pickers), chart components built with Recharts, animation components with Tailwind CSS integration, and custom React hooks for state management and lifecycle operations. Each component follows best practices for accessibility, performance, and developer experience, with comprehensive TypeScript definitions and Next.js compatibility. The platform emphasizes flexibility and customization, allowing developers to modify components at the source level rather than being constrained by package Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Let me compile my findings into a detailed report organized by skill, then create the plan with todos.

## 1. accessibility/SKILL.md
**Documented AND Implemented:**
- `lang="en"` on `<html>` element (app/layout.tsx)
- Some `aria-label` usage on icon buttons (components/skills-multi-select.tsx, components/ui/dialog.tsx)
- `sr-only` class for visually hidden text (components/admin/header.tsx, components/ui/dialog.tsx, components/ui/sheet.tsx)


- `role="status"` on spinner (components/ui/spinner.tsx)
- `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative icons

**Documented but NOT Implemented:**
- Skip link functionality, focus visible styles, and reduced motion preferences aren't in the CSS
- Missing `aria-live` regions for dynamic content updates and proper landmark elements like `<main>` on the public page
- Forms lack proper error handling with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and login form has no associated labels

Now I'm checking the AGENTS documentation against what actually exists in the codebase. Several referenced components don't exist yet—skip-link, web-vitals, and animated-section—and there are documented directories like `lib/queries/` and `lib/schemas/` that aren't present. The test:e2e script is listed in the docs but missing from package.json, and there are workflow files referenced that I need to verify are actually set up.

Moving to the better-auth implementation, I can see the core authentication setup is properly documented and implemented—the betterAuth config with Drizzle adapter, email/password authentication with signup disabled, session caching, and the auth client are all in place. The server-side session helper uses React's cache for optimization, and the API route handler is set up correctly.

However, there are some gaps: the environment variables for BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and URL aren't explicitly documented in the setup guide even though they're auto-read, rate limiting and trusted origins aren't configured, and the codebase isn't leveraging the type inference utilities that better-auth provides.

For Drizzle, the schema is properly structured with SQLite tables and relations defined, including junction tables for many-to-many relationships. The Kit config is in place with snake_case casing, and migrations are handled through the setup script. The main inconsistency is that manual types are being used instead of Drizzle's built-in type inference, and transactions haven't been implemented yet.

The frontend design skill is mostly undocumented in practice—the public page is completely empty with no design patterns implemented, and the admin dashboard only has basic styling without any distinctive visual identity. For Next.js best practices, the app is following the modern patterns correctly: using the App Router, defaulting to Server Components, applying "use client" selectively, and leveraging async params with the Geist font from next/font/google.

However, there are significant gaps in error handling and caching strategies. The project hasn't implemented error boundaries, not-found pages, loading states, or Suspense boundaries, and the HTML tag is missing the suppressHydrationWarning attribute that's recommended for theme providers. While cacheComponents is enabled in the config to support Partial Pre-Rendering, there are no actual 'use cache' directives, cacheLife calls, or cacheTag usage anywhere in the codebase, so the PPR capability isn't being leveraged.

The app router patterns are partially in place with route groups, server components, and server actions, but streaming patterns, generateMetadata, generateStaticParams, and proper loading states haven't been implemented. The Playwright setup exists with a config file and e2e directory, but only contains an example test pointing to an external site rather than testing the actual application, and the test script is missing from package.json. For SEO, the lang attribute is set to English, though the metadata implementation appears incomplete. The Form component from react-hook-form and Zod validation isn't set up yet, and while the select component is installed, it's not integrated with form handling. For Tailwind, the v4 configuration is mostly correct with the PostCSS setup and CSS variables in place, but there's no ThemeProvider wrapper to handle dark mode switching at runtime.

Looking at the TypeScript setup, strict mode is enabled and basic types are defined, but the code isn't leveraging Drizzle's type inference helpers or using discriminated unions for better type safety in server actions. The composition patterns are starting to take shape with separate components, though there's still work to do on more advanced patterns.

For React best practices, the project correctly uses Server Components as the default with Client Components only where necessary, but it's missing critical Suspense boundaries for streaming and the Server Actions lack authentication checks. There's also some cleanup needed around console statements in production code and implementing dynamic imports for better performance.

Vitest is configured with the necessary plugins and jsdom environment, but there are no actual test files written yet despite having a test script defined.

Looking at the WCAG audit patterns, I'm seeing the same accessibility gaps as before—the basics like language attributes and some ARIA are there, but skip links, error boundaries, focus indicators, and proper form validation patterns are all missing.

The web design guidelines skill is different since it's a review-on-demand tool that validates against external guidelines rather than checking for specific code implementations, so that doesn't apply to this audit.

Now I'm ready to compile everything into a consolidated report and map out the remediation plan.</details></think>
